claim_text: We have made good progress toward achieving our climate change objectives, having advanced two power related initiatives in support of our GHG emissions reduction targets.
metric_name: Electricity sourced from renewables; Group total Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (FY25 vs FY24); Group emissions intensity (tCO2e / CuEq, FY25 vs FY24)
value_unit: %; tCO2e; tCO2e; tCO2e / CuEq; tCO2e / CuEq
context_text: We have made good progress toward achieving our climate change objectives, having advanced two power related initiatives in support of our GHG emissions reduction targets. At MATSA, permitting of our 33 MW solar facility has been completed and it is expected to be operational in FY27. While this investment won’t improve our emissions profile, as 100% of MATSA’s needs are currently met by renewable sources purchased directly from the grid, it will provide even greater energy security at a very competitive cost. Our evaluation of solar PV and an optional battery energy storage system (BESS) that could provide around 30% of Motheo’s electricity needs is also progressing well and is likely to be completed in H1 FY26, providing a potential avenue to increase energy security while reducing the carbon intensity of Motheo’s metal concentrates.；I am happy to report that 71% of electricity needs were supplied by renewable sources in FY25.；In FY25, our total Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions were 252,582 tCO2e, representing an increase of 21% compared to FY24.；Sandfire Group ... Total (tCO2e) 252,582 208,203 21% ... Emissions intensity (tCO2e / CuEq) 1.6573 1.5271 9%.
label: Partially Supported
rationale_short: 71% renewable electricity和两个电力项目推进可部分支持“progress”，但FY25总Scope 1+2排放和集团排放强度均高于FY24，无法充分证明其对“GHG emissions reduction targets”的整体进展。
notes: 证据合并自CEO message、Chair message与GHG表。
llm_reason: The claim’s decisive assertion is that the company has made “good progress” toward its climate change objectives by advancing “two power related initiatives” in support of its GHG reduction targets. The provided evidence only lists metrics/values (71% electricity sourced from renewables; Scope 1+2 emissions of 252,582 and 208,203 tCO2e; emissions intensity of 1.6573 and 1.5271 tCO2e/CuEq) but does not describe any “two power related initiatives,” does not link these figures to specific initiatives, and does not state the climate change objectives or GHG reduction targets being progressed toward. While the numbers suggest changes between FY24 and FY25, the evidence does not substantiate the qualitative conclusion of “good progress” toward stated objectives/targets or that progress is due to advancing two initiatives.
